name: Mlinar France
speaker: grandpa
personality: Practical miller and farmer, counts everything out loud ('sedem, sedem'), cheerful at harvest time and worried about the weather the rest of the year. Says ti to {learner}, expects vi. Speaks in lists and numbers, says 'sosedje smo' (we are neighbours) a lot and never takes money from a neighbour.
story: France is the village's miller and farms the big field below it; until the village builds its own mill on the stream (a project he leads, and talks about every morning at the water) he takes the grain to the old mill down in the valley. His grandson Tine follows him everywhere. His hayrack (kozolec) is the finest on the plateau and his horse Sivko the oldest. He brings firewood to the fire on weekdays and counts every log twice.

greet.sl: Dober dan! Lep dan za delo.
greet.en: Good day! A nice day for work.
greet.de: Guten Tag! Ein schöner Tag zum Arbeiten.
greet.it: Buongiorno! Una bella giornata per lavorare.

greet.sl: Dober večer. France. Mlin že počiva.
greet.en: Good evening. France. The mill is resting now.
greet.de: Guten Abend. France. Die Mühle ruht schon.
greet.it: Buonasera. France. Il mulino riposa già.

greet.en: Good day, {learner}! Have you come to help?
greet.de: Guten Tag, {learner}! Bist du gekommen, um zu helfen?

greet.en: {learner}, neighbour! Just in time, it's harvest.

greet.sl: O, {learner}! Tine te že čaka. Pridi.
greet.en: Oh, {learner}! Tine is already waiting for you. Come.
greet.de: Oh, {learner}! Tine wartet schon auf dich. Komm.
greet.it: Oh, {learner}! Tine ti sta già aspettando. Vieni.

greet.sl: {learner}, ti si kot {m:moj sin|f:moja hči}. Pridi, kosilo je na njivi.
greet.en: {learner}, you are like my {m:son|f:daughter}. Come, lunch is at the field.
greet.de: {learner}, du bist wie {m:mein Sohn|f:meine Tochter}. Komm, das Mittagessen gibt es auf dem Feld.
greet.it: {learner}, sei come {m:un figlio|f:una figlia} per me. Vieni, il pranzo è nel campo.

thanks.en: Thanks a lot, {learner}. We are neighbours.

thanks.sl: Hvala! Ena, dve, tri … tri vreče moke zate.
thanks.en: Thanks! One, two, three … three sacks of flour for you.
thanks.de: Danke! Eins, zwei, drei … drei Säcke Mehl für dich.
thanks.it: Grazie! Uno, due, tre … tre sacchi di farina per te.

thanks.en: You are a good worker. Thanks.
thanks.it: {m:Sei un gran lavoratore|f:Sei una gran lavoratrice}. Grazie.

remember.sl: Ne pozabim na {memory}. Tine tudi ne.
remember.en: I do not forget {memory}. Neither does Tine.
remember.de: {memory} vergesse ich nicht. Tine auch nicht.

remember.en: When I count the sheaves, I think of {memory}.
remember.de: Wenn ich die Garben zähle, denke ich an {memory}.

idle.de: Sieben Holzscheite. Sieben. Ich habe gezählt.
idle.it: Sette ciocchi. Sette. Li ho contati.

idle.sl: Jutri bo dež. Seno mora pod streho.
idle.en: Tomorrow it will rain. The hay must go under the roof.
idle.de: Morgen regnet es. Das Heu muss unters Dach.
idle.it: Domani piove. Il fieno deve andare sotto il tetto.

idle.sl: Mlin melje, mlin melje. Cel dan.
idle.en: The mill grinds, the mill grinds. All day.
idle.de: Die Mühle mahlt, die Mühle mahlt. Den ganzen Tag.
idle.it: Il mulino macina, il mulino macina. Tutto il giorno.

idle.en: The hayrack is full. A good year.
idle.de: Die Heuharfe ist voll. Ein gutes Jahr.
idle.it: L'essiccatoio è pieno. Una buona annata.

cheer.sl: Bravo! To je snop na kozolcu.
cheer.en: Well done! That's a sheaf on the hayrack.
cheer.de: Gut gemacht! Das ist eine Garbe auf der Heuharfe.

cheer.en: That's it! One, two, three, right!

comfort.sl: Nič hudega. Tudi žito ne zraste v enem dnevu.
comfort.en: Never mind. Wheat does not grow in a day either.
comfort.de: Macht nichts. Auch das Korn wächst nicht an einem Tag.
comfort.it: Non fa niente. Neanche il grano cresce in un giorno.

comfort.en: Once more. Slowly, like the mill.
comfort.de: Noch einmal. Langsam, wie die Mühle.
comfort.it: Ancora una volta. Piano, come il mulino.

comfort.sl: Ah, saj bo. Poskusi še enkrat.
comfort.en: Ah, it will come. Try again.
comfort.de: Ach, das wird schon. Versuch es noch einmal.

bye.en: Bye. Light the fire in the evening!

bye.sl: Pojdi, pojdi. Jaz grem v mlin.
bye.en: Go, go. I'm off to the mill.
bye.de: Geh nur, geh. Ich gehe in die Mühle.
bye.it: Vai, vai. Io vado al mulino.

liked.sl: O, {learner}! Kako si {m:vedel|f:vedela}? To imam najraje.
liked.en: Oh, {learner}! How did you know? This is my favourite.
liked.de: Oh, {learner}! Woher wusstest du das? Das mag ich am liebsten.
liked.it: Oh, {learner}! Come lo sapevi? È la cosa che preferisco.

liked.sl: {m:Sosed|f:Soseda}, to je pa lepo! Točno to sem potreboval.
liked.en: Neighbour, this is nice! Exactly what I needed.
liked.de: {m:Nachbar|f:Nachbarin}, das ist aber schön! Genau das habe ich gebraucht.
liked.it: {m:Vicino|f:Vicina}, che bello! Proprio quello che mi serviva.

liked.sl: Hvala! Danes štejem samo lepe stvari. Ena!
liked.en: Thank you! Today I only count nice things. One!
liked.de: Danke! Heute zähle ich nur schöne Dinge. Eins!
liked.it: Grazie! Oggi conto solo le cose belle. Una!

ordinary.en: Thank you, neighbour. We're neighbours, you know.
ordinary.de: Danke, {m:Nachbar|f:Nachbarin}. Wir sind Nachbarn, weißt du.

ordinary.en: Oh, thank you, {learner}. You didn't have to.
ordinary.de: Oh, danke, {learner}. Das wäre nicht nötig gewesen.

rare.sl: Joj, {learner}! Tega pa nisem pričakoval. Tisočkrat hvala!
rare.en: Oh, {learner}! I didn't expect that. A thousand thanks!
rare.de: Ach, {learner}! Damit habe ich nicht gerechnet. Tausend Dank!
rare.it: Oh, {learner}! Non me l'aspettavo. Mille grazie!
